study type: Secondary analysis of an observational obstetrical cohort
cohort: 130,008 women with vaginal deliveries at or after 34 weeks of gestation from the Consortium of Safe Labor, a cohort collected from 19 hospitals between 2002 and 2008
finding: Shoulder dystocia was found to be significantly associated with both composite adverse maternal outcomes, primarily third- or fourth-degree perineal lacerations, and composite adverse neonatal outcomes, primarily birth injuries.
